➡️From Vintage to MNTGE: Digital Fashion Brand to Release NFT Patches Linked to IRL Rewards

Digital fashion brand MNTGE is gearing up to release its Patchwork collection, comprised of a series of non-fungible token (NFT) patches paired with a physical counterpart.

MNTGE Patchwork features 13 unique digital patches designed by 11 artists including Jen Stark, Bored Ape Yacht Club artist Seneca and Nyan Cat meme creator Christopher Torres. The entire 7,500-unit collection will open for sale on July 27 on NFT marketplace OpenSea. Each NFT will be priced at 0.07 ETH, or $130, and the artwork will be revealed upon mint.

Each NFT is linked to an identical physical patch. Embedded with a near-field communication (NFC) chip, owners can scan the real-world patch to claim the digital token in their crypto wallet. By holding the patch on the blockchain and IRL, users can trace ownership as well as attend token-gated events and exclusive MNTGE experiences.

Additionally, the patches aren’t just one-off collectibles. In the physical world, they can be sewn onto MNTGE’s “base garments,” including t-shirts, jackets and denim. In the digital realm, the patches can be “owned” by the base garment itself. By implementing an ERC-6551 token standard, the digital wearable becomes a token-bound account that can custody the patches – creating an added layer of digital ownership.

Nick Adler, co-founder of MNTGE, told CoinDesk that the company was rooted in the goal of selling vintage fashion and utilizing the blockchain to revitalize its origins.

“People are out there wearing [vintage] and collecting it…young kids want to be authentic,” said Adler. “They don't want a Hot Topic shirt, they want the original shirt, right? So we just saw this natural, really honest use case for the blockchain, and we just felt like the two could really go hand in hand.”

TON DNS Summer (Part 1)

As we predicted, the hype around TON DNS has begun. The hype began with Four-Digit domains (hereinafter referred to as 4N domains). People are "burning" their 100 TON on the TON DNS smart contract and transferring this value to NFTs (similar to Banksy's work). 

On February 13, the last domain from the Club 100 (0074.ton), was minted, on February 17, the thousandth domain (5755.ton), and on February 28, the last domain from the 1k Club (0863.ton).

The race is on, and people have already minted many beautiful numbers from various masks and special collections, although only 26% of the total supply has been minted.

On average, 117 4N domains are minted per day. At the current rate, 50% of the supply will be minted by March 22, 2026, 75% by April 12, 2026, and 100% by May 4, 2026. 

Why 4N domains if there are already Telegram usernames?

1. Numbers are the international language of communication. They are simple and understandable for everyone around the world, unlike various alphabets (be it Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic, hieroglyphs, etc.).

2. There are 10^4 = 10,000 number combinations in 4N domains, compared to 26^4 = 456,976 combinations in alphabetical ones.

3. The price for the 4L username is fixed at $8,000. The price for the 4N domain on mint is approximately $130, which is 61.54 times cheaper!

4. Only domains can consist of numbers, while usernames must contain at least one letter. Therefore, 4N domains are beyond competition in the TON ecosystem.

5. The ability to associate attractive domain digits with a gift number. An example is here. There are dozens of different collections of gifts with identical numbers, but only one 4N domain can be associated with them!

6. The TON ecosystem will have thousands of AI agents, and they will need a short digital domain for convenience.

7. TON Browser and TON Messenger are being developed, with user login via TON DNS.

8. Repeating the success of ENS, this time in the form of a utility — a shell in Telegram (because TON DNS renewal costs pennies, compared to $160 per year for a 4-digit ENS).

🚀 Want to Become a Generative AI Engineer in 2026? Here’s Your Learning Roadmap.

GenAI is evolving fast. You don’t need 50 courses or every framework. Master these 10 skills in sequence. 👇

1️⃣ Transformers & LLM Fundamentals

📄 Iran has no intention of transferring enriched uranium abroad: Diplomat

📌 Moscow, IRNA — Mojtaba Ferdowsipoor, head of the Iranian Interests Section in Cairo, has rejected the speculations that the Islamic Republic will transfer its enriched uranium abroad, stressing that the stockpile will remain in the country and under the supervision of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).

Speaking to RIA Novosti, a Russian news agency, on Tuesday, Ferdowsipoor reiterated Iran’s long-standing approach to its peaceful nuclear program, saying the country’s principled stance on the matter remains unchanged as it has no intention of transferring the enriched materials.
​
Pointing to a proposal put forward by Qatar and Pakistan aimed at bridging differences between the US and Iran, the diplomat said Tehran was carefully and seriously reviewing the draft from the two intermediaries.
​
He made, however, clear that any potential agreement with Washington must recognize Iran’s right to uranium enrichment, provide the complete and verifiable lifting of sanctions, as well as guarantees that the US would not withdraw from the agreement again, as it did in 2018.
​
The remarks come just days after Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in an interview with an Iranian newspaper that Tehran was seeking a “good, honorable and dignified agreement,” to safeguard its national interests and prevent a renewed conflict, stressing that the country would not compromise with its dignity.
​
Referring to a proposal Iran had previously presented, Araghchi said a two-day plan that followed the compression of an initial seven-day plan remained on the table to reach an agreement if the Americans were truly serious about reaching one.
​
He also emphasized that the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding is no longer on the table; rather, Iran’s proposal combining US commitments under the MoU is the basis for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and negotiations.
​
Under it, he explained, the United States would fulfill its commitments on the first day, and Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz on the second, when negotiations on a final agreement would begin.

Anthropic starts trading on the Nasdaq. And this is one of the most important events in the AI market in years.

The company priced its shares at $83, putting its valuation at around $1.5 trillion. The IPO raised more than $81 billion, making it the largest in history. Another $26 billion was invested separately by Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom, TSMC, and other companies across the same AI ecosystem.

And the timing of this listing couldn't have been better.

The day before yesterday, Nvidia once again posted insane numbers. Quarterly revenue came in at $115.8 billion, twice as much as a year ago. Data centers alone accounted for $107.6 billion. In other words, money is still pouring into AI infrastructure at an enormous scale.

But Anthropic reveals the other side of this story. The company is growing rapidly, but at the same time, it has already taken on nearly $900 billion in future commitments for computing capacity. Essentially, Nvidia and other companies are generating hundreds of billions in revenue today because Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and others keep building more data centers and buying more computing power.

And this creates a rather interesting dynamic. Nvidia sells infrastructure to Anthropic. Anthropic spends enormous amounts of money on it. And now Nvidia is also helping finance Anthropic so it can keep growing and buying even more infrastructure.

This doesn't mean demand is artificial. Anthropic's revenue is growing at an incredible pace, and demand for AI is very real. But today, for the first time, the market gets a chance to publicly value one of the biggest buyers of all this infrastructure.

That's why I wouldn't focus only on the price at which ANT opens trading today.

If Anthropic surges after its listing, the market will get yet another confirmation that investors are still willing to fund AI at practically any price.

But if one of the most anticipated IPOs of the decade starts to struggle, the questions will quickly spread to the entire supply chain. Because Nvidia's seemingly endless revenue growth is only possible as long as someone is willing to keep paying for the construction of all this infrastructure.

Today, we'll finally see how much the public market is willing to pay for it.
